internet-of-things-and-applications--iot.title: the seven Cisco IoT reference levels
rows: sensors and actuators that touch the real world
links and protocols between devices and the network
filters, aggregates and inspects packets before the core
stores arriving data, turning events into records
reconciles formats into one consistent schema
reports, control loops and business logic
people and workflows acting on the reports
internet-of-things-and-applications--iot.note: The levels are numbered upward from the devices, and each one consumes only what the level below has already cleaned up.

internet-of-things-and-applications--mqt.title: MQTT delivery guarantees
rows: at most once; may be lost
two round trips and stored state
internet-of-things-and-applications--mqt.note: Each level buys one more handshake: QoS 1 may duplicate and QoS 2 may not, which is why QoS 2 costs the most state.

internet-of-things-and-applications--mqt.title: MQTT publish through a broker
internet-of-things-and-applications--mqt.note: The two clients never address each other: the topic string is all they share and the broker owns the matching.

internet-of-things-and-applications--amq.title: IoT application protocols compared
internet-of-things-and-applications--amq.note: The choice is mostly transport plus coupling: UDP where links are weak, a broker where many readers need one writer's data.

internet-of-things-and-applications--edg.title: data path from device to cloud

steps.label: control command back to the device
aggregated summary once a minute, 2 kB

internet-of-things-and-applications--edg.note: Filtering before the WAN hop is what the reduction ratio on this row measures: less traffic, less latency, less cloud storage.

internet-of-things-and-applications--ske.title: an Arduino sketch as setup and loop
lines: pinMode(LED_BUILTIN, OUTPUT);   /* runs once after reset */
internet-of-things-and-applications--ske.note: setup() runs once after reset and loop() is called repeatedly, so a sketch never returns from loop() on its own.

internet-of-things-and-applications--blu.title: short-range radios by range and rate
internet-of-things-and-applications--blu.note: Range and rate pull in opposite directions: each step down in data rate buys roughly an order of magnitude in reach and battery life.

internet-of-things-and-applications--gpi.title: reading a GPIO pin with the BCM numbering
lines: if GPIO.input(17) == GPIO.LOW:  # button pulls the pin to ground
internet-of-things-and-applications--gpi.note: In BCM mode the number is the SoC's GPIO number rather than the header pin, so the same code survives a board revision.
